What you need to capture

What the app shows you.

Sign in with your email, practise on one small room, then check the saved route before you send anything.

Screens from the current build in the iOS Simulator; on a real iPhone the camera fills the capture screen. The app is in invite-only testing through TestFlight.

One property, five steps.

  1. Choose the space and scope.

    Decide the rooms, private areas to exclude and who reviews. One new accepted capture uses one walkthrough, regardless of room count, and each capture has its own link and QR code. A home with more rooms than fit in one capture takes more captures. Keep street addresses and access instructions out of anything you share.

  2. Prepare and capture.

    Clear personal documents and screens, keep people and pets out of the route, and keep lighting steady. Walk the space with the phone upright and follow the capture guidance. Review the saved photographs and route checks before leaving; those checks do not prove capture quality. After you send it, an automatic quality check assesses capture quality.

  3. Automatic processing and quality check.

    Send from the app: it uploads in the background. Check your account for rendering status. Veylet reconstructs it automatically. We’ll email you when it’s ready. An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work, such as one with no usable photos or depth; it retries once when a retry can help. Other findings about photo match, coverage, stray artefacts and walkable paths are flagged for you to check before approval. No person checks it, and recording on the phone does not create a finished tour by itself. Your original stays on the iPhone. A failed capture is never counted. A correction to the same walkthrough, or a permitted whole recapture including every original room, replaces it on the same link and uses no extra walkthrough.

  4. Review before sharing.

    Open the owner preview on your phone. Check every room, turns, doorways, floor and ceiling edges, privacy and phone navigation. Approve it or send one consolidated list of corrections. Each accepted walkthrough counts toward the 3 included in your free month, or toward your plan’s allowance after them. Capture permission and permission to publish are separate.

  5. Share on your terms.

    Once the tour is reviewed and sharing is enabled, copy its link or embed code from your desk. Viewers need no account or capture app. Anyone who receives the link can forward it.

    Add a tour to your agency website

Your first session: one practice capture.

For every new account.

Veylet confirms your device and app access first, and the app unlocks real captures once your practice room passes. Installation alone does not approve you for client work.

  1. Check the device and install the agreed build.With Veylet support, confirm the exact model, rear LiDAR, OS version, camera permission and available storage. Follow the installation link Veylet sends you. If the device is unsupported, stop: capture needs a supported device.
  2. Record one small, permissioned space.Read the preparation guide, clear private items and follow the current in-app movement prompts. Start with the agreed practice route. Branding, team invitations and website setup can wait.
  3. Inspect what you saved.Open the saved photographs and check coverage before leaving. A saved capture is your first setup checkpoint; it is not a finished or quality-approved tour. Keep the original if you need help or another attempt.
  4. Send it from the app.Tap Send to Veylet. Send from the app: it uploads in the background. Check your account for rendering status. We’ll email you when it’s ready. Veylet processes the capture automatically. The automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work; other findings are flagged for you to check before approval. Your original stays on the iPhone. Client work needs explicit production approval and agreed terms.

Stuck at sign-in or sending? Keep your capture and tell Veylet support which step stopped, the device model and app build. Do not include passwords, access codes or private images in an email. For capture availability, join the waitlist; sign in with the email you joined with.

Keep the handover simple.

Already admitted?

Use the email you joined with on both the website and capture app. Sign in, then save a space. Account creation does not grant production approval.

When the listing changes.

Revoke the handoff and remove its embed when the tour should stop being available. Revocation blocks new access; it cannot erase copies already downloaded. Agree hosting dates and any archive or deletion request with Veylet support.

Before you start.

What if the first result is not usable?

An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work; other findings are flagged for you to check before approval. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free: the redo corrects it on the same link and uses no walkthrough, though a new capture visit is not included. Keep the originals and report the affected area. After that, we agree a correction, a permitted whole recapture including every original room or the remedy in your scope. A correction or permitted whole recapture replaces the walkthrough on the same link and uses no extra walkthrough; any other new accepted capture is its own walkthrough and link. Sharing waits for review and approval.

Can every visitor open a tour?

Visitors use a current browser with graphics support on a phone, tablet or computer. Performance depends on the tour, device and connection. Share a direct link as a fallback for website builders that block embedded content. Portal compatibility must be checked with that portal.

Can an agency use it free?

Eligible App Store subscribers receive 1 free month with 3 accepted walkthroughs in total. They begin when the plan is activated with a payment method on file, and there is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace. The first charge is on the day they end; cancel before then and nothing is charged. App Store subscriptions renew at the price of the plan you chose, monthly or annual, unless cancelled through Apple. Invoiced service continues only under explicitly agreed and settled terms; it does not auto-renew. On the monthly Veylet plan each paid month includes 2 accepted walkthroughs, and unused ones roll over, up to 4 banked; the annual plan has 24 to use any time in the plan year. For a busier month the account owner can add a pack of 3 or 10 walkthroughs, valid 12 months, including during the free months. Check the renewal date on your account; you can cancel any time. Every walkthrough you released stays live while your plan runs; when it ends, its links keep working for 14 days, then go offline until you restart it. While capture quality is still being proven we onboard accounts in cohorts, so ask about availability before promising a client a date.

Is a walkthrough a measured survey?

No. It provides visual context for a space. It is not a measured floor plan, building survey or guarantee of condition. Keep listing photography and required property information available alongside it.
